title: TCO Sensitivity Heatmap and Ops Recommendations
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet experiments with a 3-axis sensitivity heatmap to prioritize commercial offers and operational guardrails for Private deployments (on-prem vs VPC). Aim: make it easy for sales/solutions teams to say "if the customer lands in zone X, recommend bundle Y and ops guardrail Z".

Executive summary (short):
- Build heatmaps for: (A) Reserved utilization (% of reserved GPU hours used), (B) Average request qps (throughput, normalized to tokens/sec), and (C) Support uplift (1.0 baseline, 1.2 = +20% SLA / white-glove ops).
- Identify 4 outcome zones: Cost-Advantage, Neutral, Risky (high ops), and Not Recommended (evens out to hosted).
- Sample thresholds: Reserved utilization < 45% usually flips economics to VPC/hosted; throughput > 300k tokens/sec favors on-prem high-throughput clusters; support uplift >1.4 requires dedicated SRE add-ons and changes pricing by ~18–28%.

Methodology (how this sheet is organized):
1) Inputs (top area): list of independent knobs as text fields.
   - Hardware CAPEX per rack (amortized, 36 months): e.g., $450k per 8xA100-equivalent rack.
   - Cloud equivalent per-rack monthly committed cost: $38k/mo (use for on-demand parity).
   - Reserved utilization: percent (0.0–1.0).
   - Average token/sec workload: low/med/high buckets; numerical mapping used in charts.
   - Support uplift multiplier: baseline=1.0.
   - Network/egress overhead: estimated % of total monthly cost.
2) Core formulas (text; for transparency):
   - Monthly amortized CAPEX = CAPEX / 36 + annual maintenance reserve (3%) / 12.
   - Effective monthly unit cost per token = (Monthly infra + SW license + support) / monthly tokens served.
   - Breakeven reserved-utilization = (Cloud equivalent monthly cost) / (Amortized CAPEX + SW license + baseline support) -> solved for utilization; use sample tokens/sec to convert.
3) Sensitivity engine:
   - Sweep axes: utilization [25%, 40%, 55%, 70%, 85%], throughput buckets [50k, 150k, 350k, 800k tokens/sec], support uplift [1.0, 1.2, 1.5].
   - Compute relative unit cost delta vs hosted API for each cell and draw heatmap bands.

Sample numbers & example scenarios (text-table):
- Assumptions used in sample run: rack CAPEX $450,000; amortize 36 months -> $12,500/mo rack; ops & maintenance reserve (spare parts + on-call) = $1,350/mo; SW license baseline = $5,000/mo/rack; baseline support = $4,000/mo; cloud equivalent = $38,000/mo per rack.

Scenario A: High utilization (80%), high throughput (350k tok/s), baseline support (1.0)
- Monthly tokens served (conservative conv estimate): 350k tok/s * 86,400s/day * 30 days = 907,200,000,000 tokens/mo (~907B).
- Monthly infra cost (amortized) = $12,500 + $1,350 = $13,850.
- Total monthly cost (rack-level) = 13,850 + 5,000 + 4,000 = $22,850 -> unit cost per 1M tokens = $22,850 / 907,200 = $0.0252 per 1M tokens.
- Cloud equivalent per-rack = $38,000 -> unit cost per 1M tokens = $38,000 / 907,200 = $0.0419 -> on-prem wins ~40% lower unit cost.

Scenario B: Low utilization (35%), low throughput (50k tok/s), support uplift 1.2
- Monthly tokens served: 50k * 86,400 * 30 = 129,600,000,000 tokens/mo (~129B).
- Effective monthly cost with utilization factor 0.35: treat amortized rack cost divided by utilization (i.e., need ~3 racks allocated to meet peak but used at 35% across month). Rough model: allocate ceil(1/0.35)=3 racks -> amortized cost = 3 * 13,850 = $41,550.
- Support uplift 1.2 increases support line item to 4,800/mo. Total = 41,550 + 15,000 (SW licenses for 3 racks) + 4,800 = $61,350 -> unit cost per 1M tokens = $61,350 / 129,600 = $0.4739 per 1M tokens.
- Cloud equivalent (3 racks) = 3 * 38,000 = $114,000 -> unit cost per 1M tokens = $114,000 / 129,600 = $0.88 per 1M tokens -> on-prem still cheaper in absolute, but margin and ops risk are high; when including SRE FTE/response SLAs the delta narrows or reverses.

Key observations (from the sweep runs):
- Utilization has the single biggest elasticity on unit cost — below ~45% utilization, the required rack overprovisioning kills on-prem unit economics unless customer accepts pooling across tenants.
- Support uplift (1.2–1.5) is material once combined with small scale (1–2 racks). For customers with high compliance/24x7 true SRE needs, add-on pricing should be explicit: "White-glove SRE bundle = +18% on license + explicit time-and-materials FTEs".
- Throughput/latency-sensitive workloads (high tokens/sec with low tail latency SLOs) favor localized on-prem racks even at higher support uplift because network egress and cross-region throttling add both cost and latency risk.

Operational recommendations (concrete):
1) Price bands: define three prescriptive offers based on heatmap zone: "Economy VPC, Hybrid Reserved, On-prem Dedicated". Each offer should include a short checklist of required utilization commitments and support tiers.
2) Minimum commitment policy: require either (a) utilization guarantee >= 50% OR (b) cross-tenant pooling contract for single-rack deployments to avoid 3x amortization blowups.
3) Support bundle explicitness: break support into 
   - Basic: ticketing + monthly health checks (baseline),
   - Plus: 24x7 on-call + quarterly tune-ups (+18% price uplift),
   - White-glove: SRE embed + runbook customization (+28% uplift + optional time-and-materials).
4) Offer ops mitigations to salvage low-util deals: cold-start autoscale connectors to hosted for overflow, shared caching layer, scheduled batch runs to increase utilization, or hybrid VPC bridging. Include contractual fallback to terminate dedicated hardware if utilization falls below floor for 3 months.
5) Engineering to produce a simple SLA/ops playbook for the Plus and White-glove bundles (runbook templates, on-call rotation guidance, incident cost pass-through terms).

Pricing play examples (text):
- Example customer match: e-comm search engine with 300k tok/s predictable peaks -> recommend On-prem Dedicated with Plus support and a 18-month minimum commitment with utilization target 65%.
- Example small AI-SaaS (50–150k tok/s, bursty) -> recommend Hybrid Reserved (VPC with reserved bursts + pooling) and Basic support; include auto-burst to hosted as default.

Risk register (quick list):
- Low utilization churn (most likely) -> financial exposure for Redwood and customer.
- Hidden network cost (inter-datacenter egress) -> propose a network surcharge line item.
- Hardware refresh mismatch -> customers may need earlier refresh than 36mo; include buyback/upgrade credits in contract.

Visualization guidance (for deck/sales):
- Produce 3 heatmap images: one per support uplift bucket (1.0/1.2/1.5). X axis = utilization buckets, Y axis = throughput buckets. Color = relative unit-cost delta vs hosted.
- Superimpose recommended offer boundary lines and short tooltips: "Recommend On-prem here" or "Recommend Hybrid/Host fallback".

Next steps / action items (owners + short timeline):
- Product (Maya P) 2 weeks: finalize param list & canonical macros; ship the canonical spreadsheet in the sales playbook.
- Solutions Eng (Diego A) 3 weeks: create 2 ready-to-run customer templates (high-throughput, low-utilization) + 1 onboarding checklist.
- Engineering (Owen R) 4 weeks: instrument infra cost telemetry so we can measure realized utilization across customer fleets and fold back into models.
- Pricing (Aisha K) 2 weeks: draft explicit SRE bundle pricing and contract language for utilization floor.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Confirm hardware amortization window (24 vs 36 vs 48 months) for regulated customers who demand faster refresh.
- Decide whether to allow 'grace pooling' for first 90 days for new customers before enforcing utilization floors.
- Should we create a small "pilot-support credit" to encourage customers to sign on even if initial utilization looks low? (tradeoff: may distort signals).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Could simulate a "pooled cluster offering" for multiple small customers in the same VPC segment to avoid 3x rack waste; need legal review (data isolation).
- Consider adding a networking tax metric (e.g., $/M tokens for cross-region requests) to make latency-driven on-prem decisions clearer.
- Hook this sheet into Redwood Optimize to create automated per-customer bundle recommendations.

Appendix: quick formula cheatsheet (text)
- Monthly tokens = tokens/sec * 86,400 * 30
- Effective racks required = ceil(requested_peak_capacity / single_rack_capacity) / utilization_factor (approx; used for conservative amortization)
- Monthly amortized CAPEX = CAPEX_total / amortization_months + maintenance_reserve
- Unit cost per 1M tokens = (Total monthly cost) / (Monthly tokens / 1,000,000)

End of doc.

(Working draft — keep in Drive as canonical sensitivity-run notes; will convert to a lightweight Google Sheet once macros are validated.)
